claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in near-single-phase disordered HEAs is governed by a beneficial dynamic interaction between abrasion-induced nanocrystallization and passive-film renewal.
Mechanical abrasion induces surface nanocrystallization in the proposed HEA.
Wear produces an ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer.
Wear-induced grain refinement increases surface grain-boundary density.
Higher surface grain-boundary density accelerates passive-film formation and repair.
An ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer facilitates formation of a uniform and robust passive film.
High configurational entropy intrinsically maintains chemical homogeneity in the HEA.
High configurational entropy stabilizes elemental distribution in the bulk.
Bulk elemental homogeneity ensures that the passive film remains chemically homogeneous.
Improved passive-film stability improves corrosion resistance in an AlCoCrFeNiMo-based alloy.
Protective surface films can materially affect deformation and wear resistance in HEAs.
The combined nanocrystallization and passivation mechanism reduces localized damage and corrosion initiation.
An AlCoCrFeNiMo variant is relevant to applications involving sliding wear and corrosion.
The proposed AlCoCrFeNiMo variant begins as a near-single-phase disordered solid solution.
Compared with the matched baseline, the HEA will have a lower overall combined wear-corrosion degradation rate.
Compared with the matched baseline, the HEA will have lower normalized wear-volume loss.
Compared with the matched baseline, the HEA will exhibit lower corrosion-current density and a more noble corrosion potential.
Combined tribocorrosion degradation will be less severe than the sum of degradation measured in isolated wear and corrosion tests.
The beneficial effect holds only when mechanical stress induces nanocrystallization without disrupting the passive film faster than it can be repaired.
The proposed benefit should diminish in non-corrosive environments because passive-film formation is then irrelevant.
